title: An erase whose record write fails has already cancelled the reminders row, so reminders go off without being asked
evidence: Found during S57. The web erase runs its teardown before the record write: deleteUserData passes cancelRemindersForErase (widget-src/standalone/reminders.ts:373-380, registered at standalone/app.tsx:38) as RecordSession.deleteAllData's teardown, which runs before the flush (record-session-erase.ts deleteAllDataSession). It posts a cancel; the route deletes the row (Drive proof) or tombstones it (app/lib/reminder-v2.server.ts:428-437). When the record write then fails and the erase is put back (S57), the record still holds an active opt-in. The next schedule push, at the next load (standalone/app.tsx:89-91) or tab hide (:79), posts an update for that token; updateScheduleByToken answers false for a missing or tombstoned row (reminder-v2.server.ts:349-365), the route answers 404, and pushReminderSchedule flips the opt-in to cancelled (reminders.ts:439-441). Auto-enrolment never runs again on a cancelled opt-in (reminders.ts:288, US-17 AC4). So the push does not restore the row: the person's reminders stop, and the switch shows them off, with nothing said. The same holds for any erase that keeps its pre-erase copy after the teardown ran: a failed build of the erased file already did. One variant: when the erase adopted another copy's active opt-in (record-session-erase.ts, the reminderOptIn merge before the teardown), the put-back keeps this copy's own opt-in, so the push meets no 404 for the cancelled row and the switch still shows reminders on until a merge brings the cancelled token back by its stamp. Fix options: (a) run the teardown after the record write lands, and on its failure keep the erase and warn (changes the US-11 AC2 order, which runs it first because the cancel token lives in the file the erase removes; the erased file could carry the token until the cancel lands); (b) on a failed erase, re-enrol from the active opt-in (a new row and token, the US-23 AC2 quiet period, and a second welcome email unless suppressed); (c) say it: add 'Reminders were turned off.' to the failure words (S58). The iPhone has no server row: its reminders follow the erase epoch (ReminderScheduler), so a put-back erase leaves them on. US-11 AC2, AC4; US-17 AC4
